title: DOH hospitals have 150% bed occupancy; 10,000 health workers needed

blocks.text: Hospitals of the Department of Health (DOH) are overcrowded at 150% bed occupancy rate following the implementation of the zero balance billing policy, with 10,000 healthcare worker positions still vacant at these facilities.

During the interpellation of the DOH's budget at the plenary session on Friday, Senate President Pro Tempore Tito Sotto asked how much the zero balance billing policy also raised the number of patients at DOH hospitals.
The DOH, through its budget sponsor Senator JV Ejercito, affirmed that there was an increase.

"For zero balance billing, the ones that availed of the zero balance billing programs in DOH hospitals is about 4.2 million patients," Ejercito said regarding the government health policy which seeks to remove out-of-pocket expenses of Filipinos for health services.

Ejercito added that there were also 400 beneficiaries for zero balance billing in local government unit (LGU) hospitals during the fourth quarter of the year. The number was low since the establishment of zero balance billing in LGU hospitals was recent.
EXPLAINER: Zero Balance Billing, No Co-Payment Policy — What they mean for patients

Under the zero balance billing policy, PhilHealth members confined in ward or basic accommodations are not required to pay out-of-pocket expenses for medical services covered by their PhilHealth benefits.
Procedures, operations, and medicines covered by PhilHealth should also be provided without additional charges in wards of basic rooms.
All PhilHealth members, regardless of socioeconomic status, are eligible to avail of zero balance billing.
Asked about the bed occupancy rate, Ejercito said "on the average or 'yung mga estimate po talaga mga 150% (on the average or the estimate, it is really 150%.)"

Ejercito said the DOH was seeking the Senate’ help to better capacitate provincial and LGU hospitals to help decongest the DOH hospitals. Private hospitals are also being engaged to allot 10% for their beds for zero balance billing.
Later on, Sotto said many doctors, nurses and health care workers leave for jobs abroad. He asked how many positions in DOH hospitals are unfilled because of the workers who leave.
“Ang unfilled positions talaga for healthcare workers, kasama na po 'yung nurses and others, for DOH hospitals mga 10,000 na ang kailangan,” Ejercito said.
(The unfilled positions for healthcare workers, including the nurses and others, for DOH hospitals, there are around 10,000 needed.)

To alleviate this, Ejercito said that the DOH had a ladderized program to allow healthcare workers to get promoted and improve their positions. The agency was also talking with state universities and colleges to have more healthcare scholarships so that there is a tie-in agreement to return service. — VDV, GMA News
